Title: Tracing sampling & span design for tokenized inference
Purpose:
- Capture a pragmatic tracing model for Redwood inference traffic (hosted, dedicated, private) that balances observability signal, storage cost, and query performance.
- Provide concrete span naming, attribute conventions, and sampling rules for inference requests that produce many internal events (token decode, KV cache ops, batching).
- Outline dashboards and alerts that rely on these signals without requiring full token-level traces by default.
Background and motivation:
- LLM inference introduces high cardinality and high-volume telemetry: many internal events per single API request (per-token or per-chunk). Storing every token span at full fidelity is expensive and noisy.
- Our goal: keep high-fidelity traces for a representative sample and failures, and lightweight traces for bulk traffic so dashboards and SLOs remain accurate.
High-level strategy:
1) Two-tier tracing model
   - full-trace (sample_rate_full): captures all spans for a request (parent request span + decode/token spans + cache hits + kernel events). Keep low (e.g., 2-5%).
   - thin-trace (sample_rate_thin): captures only top-level request span + aggregated metrics (per-request decode_count, tokens_emitted, batch_size). Keep higher (e.g., 20%).
   - forced-capture rules: always capture full-trace for requests that meet certain criteria (errors, p95 latency, high-cost model usage, or QA customers).

2) Tail-based sampling
   - Configure agent/collector to prefer capturing traces that are high latency or error-producing (tail-sampling). Example: if request_latency > 95th percentile OR request_status != 200 => upgrade to full-trace.

3) Aggregation vs raw spans
   - For production dashboards, compute histograms and counters from aggregated fields attached to request span (tokens_emitted, decode_chunks, batch_size) rather than summing token spans.
Span naming and hierarchy (convention):
- Top-level (parent) span: service=inference, name: request
  - Attributes: model_name, model_variant, model_quant (e.g., fp16, int8), region, customer_tier, request_type (generation|embed|rerank), prompt_hash (sha256 truncated), seq_len_input, max_tokens, billing_project
- Child spans (sparse, when thin-trace or full):
  - inference.dispatch (routing + queueing)
  - inference.cache.lookup (kv cache)
  - inference.decode.chunk (grouped token emits — one span per chunk, not per token)
  - inference.kernels.run (GPU kernel boundary for a decoder step group)
  - inference.batch.join (time spent waiting to form a batch)
- Error span: inference.error (attach error_class, error_message_redacted)
Attribute guidance (labels):
- model_name (string) — curated list; avoid free-text variants where possible
- model_variant (string) — e.g., 7b-v2, 13b-qlora
- prompt_hash (string) — hashed to avoid PII leakage
- customer_tier (string) — hosted/free|paid|enterprise
- region (string)
- seq_len_input (int)
- tokens_emitted (int)
- batch_size (int)
- kv_cache_hit (bool) or kv_cache_hits (int)
- gpu_id / host (string) — useful for hardware hotspots
Redaction rules:
- Never store raw prompt text in traces or attributes.
- If a trace collector receives prompt text, immediately hash and throw away plaintext.
- Error_message_redacted should keep a short fingerprint only (no user PII or prompt snippets).
Sampling parameters (suggested starting:
- sample_rate_full = 0.03 (3% of requests)
- sample_rate_thin = 0.20 (20% of requests get only top-level span)
- tail-sampling promotion window: examine latency and error flags across 30s buffer; promote if > 95th latency or status >= 500
- budget caps: at most 200 full traces/min per region by default; dynamic scaling allowed for incident capture
Metrics derived from traces (metric name:
- inference_request_total (counter) — increment on each top-level request accepted
- inference_request_duration_seconds (histogram) — parent request duration; buckets tuned for model class (0.01,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1,2,5,10,30)
- inference_tokens_emitted_total (counter) — tokens returned to user
- inference_batch_size (histogram) — distribution of batch sizes; use for batching efficiency
- inference_kv_cache_hits_total / inference_kv_cache_lookups_total (counters) — compute kv_cache_hit_ratio as hits/lookups
- inference_active_workers (gauge) — current number of worker processes serving inference
- inference_traces_captured_total (counter) — counts of full-trace captures (for billing/observability cost)
Dashboard panels (notes for dashboard ow:
- Traffic & cost overview
  - request rate (per-model), tokens emitted rate, estimated token compute cost (tokens * cost_per_token)
- Latency heatmap
  - p50/p90/p99 by model_variant and by seq_len_input bucket, show trend over 24h
- Batching efficiency
  - batch_size distribution, average latency vs batch_size, dropped_wait_time (time batches wait to fill)
- Cache effectiveness
  - kv_cache_hit_ratio over time per model + cache lookup latency
- Error waterfall
  - errors by class and trace examples (link to full traces when available)
- Tracing budget
  - full-traces/min, thin-traces/min, % promoted by tail-sampling, approximate storage MB/day
Alerting (starter thresholds \u2014 tune:
- High p99 latency: p99(latency) > model_class_threshold for 5min => P1 pager
- Error spike: error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m => P1 if errors are 5xx; otherwise P2
- Tracing budget exceeded: full-traces/min > 200 (or configured cap) => notify observability team
- Batch size collapse: median batch_size drops by > 50% concurrently with latency increase => investigate scheduling/queueing
Runbook snippets (quick actions):
1) On P99 latency alert
   - Check model_variant p99, compare with previous deploy window
   - Look at batching dashboard: batch_size, queueing wait
   - Look at node-level GPU saturation (gpu_util, memory_pressure)
   - If new deploy suspected, rollback model_variant to previous canary
   - If capacity issue, scale Dedicated pools or promote fallback model
   - Collect representative trace IDs (force full-trace capture) and attach to incident

2) On error spike
   - Check error classes in dashboard; find common error_message_fingerprint
   - If cache-related: check kv_cache_hit_ratio and errors from cache nodes
   - If network related: check region routing and transport errors
   - Escalate to runtime infra if host-level faults present
Data retention & cost considerations:
- Full traces: retain 30 days by default, then archive to cheaper storage for 180 days.
- Thin traces / agg metrics: retain metrics at full resolution for 90 days, downsample to 1h for 365 days.
- Provide a monthly budget telemetry report to SRE + FinOps showing MB/day and projected cost per 10k requests.
Open questions / TODOs:
- Per-customer sampling overrides: how to allow customers to opt-in to higher fidelity without exposing others? (Ticket: INF-4123)
- Should we collapse token spans into periodic checkpoints (e.g., one span per 16 tokens) for a middle ground? Run experiment INF-4201.
- How to expose prompt similarity fingerprinting safely for debugging (without prompt content)? Design doc needed (confluence: INF-tracing-design)
Notes / context for reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and aims to be implementable in the agent and collector layers (OpenTelemetry + internal tail sampler). Expect follow-up PRs in the collector repo and runtime SDK.
- Please review sampling rates and caps with FinOps and SRE for budget constraints.
Last modified reasoning:
- Primary focus: reduce cardinality in tracing while keeping actionable signal for SLOs and incidents.
- Prefer promoting (tail-sampling) over naive higher sampling; this captures anomalies without high baseline cost.
